text: Looking in they saw a quiet room. <break time="0.8s" /> With a glowing fire, a singing kettle. <break time="0.8s" /> And tea things laid out on the table. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Lay the body of Edward Hyde. <break time="0.8s" /> Dressed in clothes far too large for him. <break time="0.8s" /> Clothes of the doctors size. <break time="0.8s" /> A broken little bottle in his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And a strange smell in the air. <break time="0.8s" /> Told them that he had taken poison. <break time="0.8s" /> We have come too late. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether to save or to punish. <break time="0.8s" /> Said Utterson. <break time="0.8s" /> And now we must find the body of your master. <break time="0.8s" /> They searched every corner of the building. <break time="0.8s" /> Even the dusty cellar. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no trace of Henry Jekyll. <break time="0.8s" /> Either dead or alive. <break time="0.8s" /> On the table stood small piles of white salt. <break time="0.8s" /> Which Poole recognized as the same drug. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had always been bringing his master. <break time="0.8s" /> On the desk lay a large envelope. <break time="0.8s" /> Addressed to Utterson. <break time="0.8s" /> And inside was a new will in which Hydes name had been replaced. <break time="0.8s" /> By Uttersons own. <break time="0.8s" /> There was also a short note. <break time="0.8s" /> Dated that very day. <break time="0.8s" /> Which asked Utterson. <break time="0.8s" /> To read Doctor Lanyons story first. <break time="0.8s" /> And then Jekylls own confession. <break time="0.8s" /> Telling Poole to say nothing yet. <break time="0.8s" /> Utterson put the sealed packet in his pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And went back to his office. <break time="0.8s" /> To read the two stories in quiet.
